title: Indian Startup Funding: A Quiet Week, a Chip Seed Round and Space Bets
topic: Startup funding announced in the last 24 hours

transcript.text: Indian startup funding just hit its slowest week of the year, yet chips and satellites are still drawing serious money.
Welcome to the show.
It's Monday, the sixteenth of November, twenty twenty six, and this is your rundown of startup funding news from the last day or so.
Let's begin with the big picture.
According to YourStory, weekly venture funding into Indian startups fell to its lowest level of the year in the week of the seventh to the fourteenth of November.
Just twenty six million dollars across eleven deals.
The week before, it was two hundred sixty three million.
The previous low this year was sixty six million dollars, in the last week of May.
YourStory points to the festive period, thin deal flow, reliance on overseas capital and trade tensions.
It also puts funding from January to October at ten point four billion dollars, against twelve point one billion in all of twenty twenty five, and says this year is unlikely to beat last year.
Those are YourStory's own tallies, and other trackers may differ.
Now to the deals, starting with deep tech, where the money is going.
New Delhi chip startup Bharat Semi has raised a twenty four million dollar seed round.
That's roughly two hundred fifteen crore rupees.
The company builds programmable AI image sensors that capture and process images on a single chip.
Investors include Info Edge, South Park Commons and IndusBridge Ventures.
TechCrunch broke the story, with co-founder Vrinda Kapoor speaking to the outlet.
The company was founded in late twenty twenty one and has about seventy five staff in India and the United States.
It is pre-revenue, and its first sensors are still at prototype stage.
It targets first commercial production in twenty twenty seven, and says its approach could cut system costs by at least seventy percent.
In space, Dhruva Space is set to raise one hundred forty seven crore rupees, about fifteen and a half million dollars, in a pre-Series B round.
According to regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr, IndusBridge Ventures leads with sixty crore.
The government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund adds nearly forty seven crore, its second cheque after sixty crore in July.
Entrackr estimates the post-money valuation at around twenty two hundred crore rupees, or about two hundred thirty million dollars.
That figure is Entrackr's estimate, not confirmed by the company.
Revenue rose nearly eight times to seventy nine crore in the last financial year, while losses widened twenty one percent to about forty seven crore.
The money is meant for communication, earth observation and remote sensing satellites.
Space also featured in a report from Mint.

Citing three unnamed people, it says Jio Platforms has started talks with Skyroot Aerospace, ISRO and other Indian firms to launch satellites for a planned constellation of roughly sixteen hundred low-earth-orbit satellites.
Jio is also reportedly talking to SpaceX, but wants to try domestic options first.
Rocket capacity is seen as a hurdle.
None of this has been confirmed by the companies.
Skyroot recently became India's first spacetech unicorn.
Supporting that theme, Oister Global has launched a growth-stage Deep Tech Fund.
It targets four hundred crore rupees, with a two hundred crore greenshoe, for up to six hundred crore.
It will back eight to ten companies in areas like space, defence, semiconductors and quantum, with cheques of up to one hundred crore each.
Next, a different kind of financing.
Pune logistics firm Xpressbees has raised one hundred crore rupees in debt from BlackSoil, according to Entrackr.
It's structured as non-convertible debentures with a thirteen and a half percent annual coupon and a three-year tenure, for working capital.
In the last financial year, revenue was flat at about twenty eight hundred seventy four crore, and the net loss widened to three hundred seventy crore.
On the public markets side, Razorpay has received SEBI clearance for its IPO, with final observations issued on the third of November.
That's a few days old, but the news spread over the weekend.

Media reports, not confirmed by the company, suggest an issue of roughly five to six and a half thousand crore rupees, a valuation near five billion dollars, and a listing in the first quarter of twenty twenty seven.
Razorpay has not disclosed the issue size.
A few smaller rounds.
Bengaluru's Venomics AI raised a two point seven million dollar pre-seed.
Desible dot AI raised thirty two crore rupees led by Prime Venture Partners.
And mistEO raised an eighteen crore seed round.
Also, PlatinumRx is reportedly negotiating a round of about thirty two million dollars led by Sofina Ventures.
That's a report of talks, not a closed deal.
Abroad, Tech.eu reports about two point three billion euros in European deals last week, including a thirty million dollar Series A for Munich's SE3, led by Accel.
To wrap up: it was a very thin week for Indian venture funding, but chips, space and deep tech are still pulling in the larger cheques.
Watch whether the Razorpay IPO and the Jio satellite talks revive momentum.
